anomalies.description: A sudden, violent detonation occurs at the target location, producing a large, rapidly expanding plume of debris and smoke visible in thermal imaging.

A large plume of dark smoke and debris erupts from the left side of the frame, rapidly expanding outward—consistent with a ground-level explosion. The initial burst is visible at f0 (12.0 s) and continues to expand through f3 (13.5 s), with the most intense expansion occurring between 12.0–13.0 s.; A second, smaller but distinct explosion occurs near the center-left of the frame, evidenced by a sudden bright flash (not directly visible due to night-vision green tint) followed by a rapidly rising dust/smoke cloud that obscures the ground. This event begins around f4 (14.0 s) and is clearly developing through f8 (16.0 s).; A large plume of dark smoke erupts rapidly from the left side of the frame, indicating a sudden blast event consistent with an explosion.; The smoke cloud continues to expand and rise, with visible turbulent motion and debris dispersion, confirming the ongoing aftermath of the initial explosion.

A figure appears to be lying on the ground while another figure is positioned over them in a manner consistent with physical assault; the scene remains static with minimal movement, suggesting sustained control or subjugation rather than mutual combat.

A person is seen on the ground, apparently incapacitated or restrained, with a dark plume (likely dust/debris or smoke) rising from their vicinity; they remain largely immobile while being tracked by targeting reticles across multiple frames, suggesting an ongoing attack on a helpless individual.

A sudden, violent detonation occurs at the target location, producing a rapidly expanding fireball and smoke plume visible in thermal imaging. The initial impact (f0) shows a bright flash and debris ejection; by f1–f2, the blast cloud expands significantly, obscuring the target. The event is consistent with a high-explosive munition impact.; Secondary effects of the explosion persist: a large, turbulent smoke/debris cloud continues to expand and settle over the target area. Structural remnants become partially visible through the dissipating cloud (f4–f8), indicating destruction of a vehicle or structure. No further detonations occur, but the aftermath remains dynamic through f15.; A large, rapidly expanding plume of dark smoke and debris erupts from a central point on the ground, consistent with a high-energy explosion. The fireball/blast core is initially bright and turbulent (f0–f3), then transitions into a rising, billowing smoke column that obscures the impact site (f4–f15). The shape and dynamics are characteristic of an explosive event rather than sustained fire or controlled burn.
